proof: `Fiscal Year 2011 Abstract of Assessments`, the third table on `BOARD OF ASSESSORS`, PDF page 10 of the FY2012 annual town report, printed folio 7. Read off the page's own 518 dpi bitmap; no recognition. THE PRINTED COLUMN HEADER, READ OFF THE PAGE (rule 13b.4), is `Property Class Code/Description` | `Accts` | `Class Valuation` | `Avg.Value`. WHAT PROVES IT: the twelve classes foot to the printed TOTALS `Class Valuation` of 1,120,966,561 EXACTLY, no tolerance -- and that is the same figure the table ABOVE it reaches by a different route, from five property classes instead of twelve. THE ACCTS TOTAL IS THE TOWN'S OWN DISAGREEMENT AND IS ATTESTED, NOT MENDED: the twelve printed counts sum to 5,351 and the TOTALS row prints 5,185. Both are real figures in this report -- the `Valuation and Tax History` on the SAME PAGE prints 5,351 accounts for FY2012 and 5,185 for FY2011 -- so the row reads as FY2011's account count printed under FY2012's class detail, under a heading that says `Fiscal Year 2011`. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: which of the two the table is meant to be. The class valuations are FY2012's total to the dollar, which argues the DETAIL is FY2012; the heading and the accts total argue FY2011. Nothing on the page settles it and nothing here chooses -- a residual equal to one plausible misread is exactly the digit that must not be picked (rule 14), and 166 is not that: every count was re-read at full scale off a crop of this block. `Avg.Value` is recorded as printed and is NOT checked: the page divides inconsistently -- 64,741,400 / 435 = 148,831.9 prints as 148,831 and 23,951,500 / 86 = 278,505.8 prints as 278,506 -- so rounding is not a rule this table follows and asserting one would be our claim.
